note: Sample test questions for the New Joiner Academy (placeholders: the real questions and format are still to be decided and will be edited through admin.html). Same shape as academy.questions in km-data.js: o = options, a = index of the correct option, why = explanation. The test page must shuffle the option order each time so the answer is not always in the same position.

questions.q: Where do you find the meaning of an abbreviation such as LC or SBLC?
o: The Glossary in the Knowledge Centre
questions.why: The Glossary lists the common terms and abbreviations.

questions.q: In the service taxonomy, what is an L2?
o: A tower such as Finance & Accounting
A process area such as Order to Cash
A specific service such as Credit Management
questions.why: L0 is the tower, L1 the process, L2 the service and L3 the function.

questions.q: What does the coloured dot next to a service in the taxonomy show?
o: How much content is available for it
questions.why: Covered, Partial or Not started describes how much knowledge content exists.

questions.q: Where do you see who owns a Knowledge Centre page?
o: The “Page owner” field at the top of the page
questions.why: Page owner, Ask the expert and Approved by are shown at the top of each service page.

questions.q: A document is marked “Require access”. What does that mean?
o: You need permission before you can open it
questions.why: Require access means the content is restricted. Follow the access request steps.

questions.q: Who do you contact when a Knowledge Centre page looks wrong or outdated?
o: Use “Suggest an edit” or contact the page owner
questions.why: Readers do not edit content. The page owner and the admin team keep it correct.

questions.q: What is the best use of shadowing time?
o: Observe live work and note down questions
Fix problems in the live process
Skip it if the SOP is clear
questions.why: Shadowing is for observing and collecting questions.

questions.q: You hit a problem a process step does not cover. What do you check first?
o: Exception Handling for that step, then the “Escalate to” contact
questions.why: Exception Handling lists the situation, the action and who to escalate to.

questions.q: Why do SLAs and KPIs matter in day-to-day work?
o: They show what good looks like and when to escalate
questions.why: They set the expected quality and timing.

questions.q: What should you do when you still need support after week 12?
o: Tell your manager and use the Knowledge Centre to find the right contact
questions.why: Raise gaps early and use the Ask the expert contact on the page.

questions.q: Which Knowledge Centre page holds the LC review pilot content?
questions.why: The LC review pilot sits under 3.1.1 Credit Management.

questions.q: An LC charges split (field 71D) differs from the sales contract. What is the first step?
o: Request an amendment through Customer Operations
Pay the charges and report later
questions.why: See the exception handling item for the charges split.

questions.q: Which LC field covers additional conditions?
questions.why: 47A is Additional Conditions. 71D is Charges.

questions.q: Which two teams work together in the LC review and consultation step?
questions.why: CO and Finance share this step in the workflow.

questions.q: The payment method decision can lead to which outcome?
o: Credit limit, LC or cash in advance
questions.why: The risk assessment leads to a credit limit, an LC (or SBLC) or CIA.

questions.q: Which L2 service covers shipping the order?
questions.why: Fulfil Orders includes processing and shipping the order.

questions.q: Who do you involve when an LC clause needs review?
o: Finance, through the LC review process
questions.why: LC review and consultation is shared between CO and Finance.

questions.q: Which L2 service covers proforma invoices?
questions.why: Billing & Invoicing includes creating and releasing invoices.

questions.q: Where do you find follow-up steps for overdue payments?
questions.why: Collection Management covers overdue payments.

questions.q: A customer order is delayed. Where do you start looking for guidance?
o: The Fulfil Orders page and its exception handling
questions.why: Start from the service page that matches the process step.

questions.q: Which L2 service covers Request to Purchase?
questions.why: 2.1.4 is Request to Purchase.

questions.q: Where are agreements with vendors managed?
questions.why: Outline agreements sit under 2.1.3.

questions.q: Which service covers one-off purchases?
questions.why: Spot Buy covers one-off purchases.

questions.q: Which L2 service covers vendor master data for purchase orders?
questions.why: Vendor data for PO sits under 2.1.1.

questions.q: You need to run a sourcing event. Where do you start?
questions.why: Sourcing activities sit under 2.2.2.

questions.q: Which L2 service covers employee master data?
questions.why: Employee master data sits under 4.1.1.

questions.q: An employee record has a data quality issue. Where do you look first?
o: The exception handling and data quality checks for 4.1.1
questions.why: Data quality checks are a function of 4.1.1.

questions.q: Which service covers screening and shortlisting candidates?
questions.why: Recruitment includes screening and shortlisting.

questions.q: Which service covers payroll cut-off dates?
questions.why: Payroll cut-off coordination sits under 4.1.3.

questions.q: You must prepare payroll data on your own. Where do you find the steps?
questions.why: The service page links to the SOPs and guides.

questions.q: You are following one process end to end. Where do you start?
o: The L2 service page and its process map
An old email from a colleague
questions.why: The L2 page shows the process steps and the knowledge for each step.

questions.q: What does a highlighted step on the business process map mean?
o: It is covered by the current KM pilot
questions.why: The highlighted step is the one covered by the current KM pilot.

questions.q: While shadowing you notice a step that differs from the SOP. What should you do?
o: Note it down and raise it with the page owner or expert
questions.why: Readers do not edit content. The page owner and the expert keep it correct.

questions.q: Which two sources do you use when practising a step?
o: The SOP and the quick reference guide
questions.why: The SOP gives the steps and the quick reference guide is the checklist.

questions.q: What does the complexity rating (Low, Medium, High) on an exception tell you?
o: How involved the situation is and how soon to escalate
questions.why: Exception Handling items list the situation, complexity, action and who to escalate to.

questions.q: During supervised execution, what is the reviewer’s role?
o: Check your work and give feedback before it is final
questions.why: You do the step and someone reviews it.

questions.q: A page is marked Draft. What does that mean?
o: The content is still being worked on and is not approved yet
questions.why: Draft, In review and Approved show how far content is through approval.

questions.q: You need guidance on a task you have not done before. What is the fastest route?
o: Search the Knowledge Centre and open the matching service page
Wait for your manager to explain
Guess based on a similar task
questions.why: Search or browse to the L2 service, then to the process step.

questions.q: What makes a good readiness reflection?
o: What I can do on my own and where I still need support
A list of every document I opened
questions.why: It helps you and your manager plan the support you still need.

questions.q: What is the first step on the Credit Management process map?
questions.why: The map starts with the customer risk assessment, then the payment method decision.

questions.q: Which LC field lists the documents required for presentation?
questions.why: 46A lists documents required, 45A the goods and 48 the presentation period.

questions.q: A 47A condition needs several review passes between CO and Finance. How is it rated in the pilot?
questions.why: See the exception handling item for additional conditions.

questions.q: In Fulfil Orders, which function comes first?
questions.why: 1.1.4.1 Processing the orders comes before 1.1.4.2 Shipping the order.

questions.q: Where do you find creating a credit or debit note and approving it?
questions.why: Credit and debit notes are a function of Billing & Invoicing.

questions.q: Which service covers system adjustments for delinquent account balances?
questions.why: This is function 1.1.6.1 under Collection Management.

questions.q: Which function comes first under Spot Buy?
o: Generate and issue a Purchase Order
questions.why: 2.1.7.1 is the first function of Spot Buy.

questions.q: Which function comes first under Vendor Data Management (PO)?
o: Establish vendor master data policies and guideline
questions.why: 2.1.1.1 comes first.

questions.q: Where would you find crisis procurement and emergency sourcing?
questions.why: This is function 2.1.6.5.

questions.q: Which service reviews a job requisition for completeness?
questions.why: This is function 4.1.2.1 under Recruitment.

questions.q: Where do you find creating, updating and validating employee records?
questions.why: This is function 4.1.1.1.

questions.q: Which function covers periodic audits of employee data accuracy and consistency?
questions.why: This is function 4.1.1.3.
